statement: Strip-based serpentine construction with 2-opt local search and carrot-aware prime placement scores ~55.45 on Frontier-CS problem 44, near the top of the 45-60 predicted range, demonstrating that geometric tour optimization combined with penalty avoidance is effective for this TSP variant.
regime: Frontier-CS problem 44 (Traveling Santa with Carrot Constraint), N up to 200K, 2.5s time limit, 20 test cases
mechanism: Strip construction groups cities into horizontal bands (sqrt(N*H/W) strips) and visits them in serpentine order, reducing expected step distance from ~H/3 (x-sorted baseline) to ~max(W,H)/sqrt(N). 2-opt with adaptive window (30 for large N, up to N for small N) eliminates crossing edges, running until 2.1s. Carrot optimization swaps prime-numbered cities to penalty positions (indices 9, 19, 29, ...) to avoid the 10% penalty multiplier on those steps.
applicability_bounds: Holds for the current test data mix (20 test cases, N from 10 to 200K). Score of 55.45 leaves room for improvement — theoretical maximum is 100 but practically limited by the scoring curve (s_full = N^0.6, tau=1.25). 2-opt window sizes are time-constrained.

statement: The 2-opt local optimum for strip-based tours is robust: ILS with double-bridge perturbation, or-opt with linked lists, edge-distance caching, and wide-first 2-opt all either matched or degraded the baseline 55.45 score, suggesting the 2-opt basin is well-converged within the 2.5s time budget.
regime: Frontier-CS problem 44, N up to 200K, 2.5s time limit
mechanism: ILS: double-bridge perturbation + re-optimize consumed time without finding better basins (~55.46). Or-opt: linked-list city relocation consumed 900ms leaving insufficient 2-opt time (55.4->52.6). Edge caching: precomputing ddist introduced a subtle buffer overrun bug at tour boundary (55.4->43.4/50.4). Wide-first 2-opt: wider initial window more expensive per pass, fewer total passes (55.4->55.3).
applicability_bounds: This robustness may break with fundamentally different construction methods (nearest-neighbor, Christofides) that start in different basins, or with LK-style moves that can escape 2-opt local optima. Significant improvement beyond ~55 likely requires a fundamentally different approach.

statement: The carrot constraint (10% penalty on every 10th step) contributes only ~1-5% of total penalized cost. Geometric tour optimization dominates score improvement.
mechanism: Approximately N/10 steps are penalty positions. Even if all are penalized, the 10% surcharge on N/10 steps adds only 1% to total cost. After geometric optimization reduces edge lengths, the absolute penalty savings from carrot swaps are small. Not directly measured via ablation in iter-1.
applicability_bounds: Estimated from the penalty structure; iter-2 should test geometry-only vs carrot-only to confirm quantitatively.
